videos.title: The AI Pilot Graveyard Is an Ops Problem
videos.angle: AI pilots fail when they are scoped like demos instead of workflow changes.
videos.why_now: Healthcare AI buyers are moving from experimentation into operational proof.

arc.hook: Most failed AI pilots do not die because the model was bad.
arc.setup: They die because nobody changed the workflow around the model.
arc.turn: The useful question is not whether the demo works. It is who acts differently on Tuesday morning.
arc.payoff: Before approving a pilot, define the owner, trigger, escalation path, and measurement window.
arc.cta: Audit one active pilot against those four fields before adding another.

timeline.voiceover: Most failed AI pilots do not die because the model was bad.
timeline.visual: Fast stack of abandoned pilot cards collapsing into a clean operations board.
timeline.on_screen_text: The pilot was not the product.

timeline.voiceover: They die because the workflow never changed. The alert fires, the team nods, and then everyone keeps doing the old process.
timeline.visual: Split screen: shiny demo on the left, unchanged clinic queue on the right.

timeline.voiceover: Before approving a pilot, ask four questions. Who owns the action? What triggers it? Where does escalation go? When do we measure the change?
timeline.visual: Four checklist blocks animate in one by one.

timeline.voiceover: If those answers are vague, you do not have an AI implementation. You have a science fair project with a budget code.
timeline.visual: Budget stamp turns into a project roadmap with accountable names.

timeline.voiceover: Take one active pilot and score it against those four fields this week.
timeline.visual: Checklist locks into a shareable scorecard.
